World.title: Tinubu: True Judicial Independence Evolves Around Dignity and Welfare of Officers
World.content:
* Says judges can’t effectively dispense justice without basic comfort, security

* Inaugurates FHC judges’ quarters

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has stressed that true judicial independence is built on the dignity and welfare of judicial officers, insisting that protecting the dignity of judges keeps the justice system shielded from manipulation and compromise.

He noted that while a well-supported judiciary is indispensable to good governance, his administration has driven comprehensive reforms to ensure the justice sector operates without hindrance.

Speaking on Wednesday while inaugurating the newly built 10 housing units judicial quarters for judges of the Federal High Court in Katampe District, Abuja, the president, who was represented by Vice-President Kashim Shettima, noted that he was not just inaugurating buildings, but fortifying a vital pillar of the Nigeria’s democracy: the Judiciary.

“True judicial independence is built on the dignity of our judicial officers. By providing these state-of-the-art residential quarters, we are ensuring that our Federal High Court Judges operate from a place of security, comfort, and utmost dignity.

“This project is a deliberate shield against vulnerability, a statement that Nigeria values those who interpret her laws,” Tinubu declared.

The president averred that providing judges with secure accommodation and conducive environments is not a privilege, but a national imperative, just as he said judges can’t be expected “to dispense justice without fear or favour if their basic comfort, security, and peace of mind are left to chance”.

Tinubu recalled that when his administration embarked on the ‘Renewed Hope Agenda’, he made a sacred covenant with the Nigerian people, promising “to rebuild institutional trust, secure our nation, and ensure that the rule of law is neither compromised nor delayed”.

“Today, with the official commissioning of these 10 housing units for judges of the Federal High Court, we are taking a definitive, physical step towards fulfilling that promise.

“For too long, we have talked about the independence of the judiciary in abstract terms. But independent thought requires an independent and secure environment,” he added.

He charged the judges to speedily dispense justice, saying the country is looking up to them.

His words: “The Renewed Hope Agenda is anchored on equity and justice. As we provide the infrastructure to make your lives easier, we ask in return for an unwavering commitment to the swift, fair, and transparent dispensation of justice.

“Let these homes be centres of deep reflection, integrity and honour. Let the judgments that emanate from your minds continue to strengthen the fabric of our democracy.”

The president commended the Minister of the FCT, Nyesom Wike, for demonstrating that performance is the only currency that matters in public service, describing him as tireless, dynamic and unapologetically focused.

According to him, “When I gave Minister Wike the assignment to transform Abuja into a world-class capital city, I knew his capacity for delivery. Nyesom Wike, you have not disappointed.

“From fixing critical road networks to ensuring the timely completion of projects like this Judges’ quarters, you have proven that performance is the only currency that matters in public service.”

Earlier, FCT Minister, Wike, said the completion of the project within the scheduled time is a reflection of President Tinubu’s commitment to the independence of the judiciary and sustenance of the rule of law in Nigeria.

While appealing to the beneficiaries of the project to ensure the maintenance of the buildings and environment, the minister said the entire section of the Katampe District, where the quarters is located, has been secured for the provision of residential accommodation for judges and senior officials of the nation’s judiciary resident in the FCT.

Also speaking, Chief Judge of the Federal High Court of Nigeria, Justice John Tsoho, who expressed delight over the inauguration of the project, said it signified the reaffirmation of a national understanding about the imperative of judicial independence.

World.title: Bok in a bakkie: Cheslin Kolbe shows off latest car
World.content:
Cheslin Kolbe is adding another monster of a ride to his car collection. The Springbok has returned to South Africa, swapping his Tokyo club Suntory Sungoliath for Cape Town’s Stormers.

According to coach John Dobson, the award-winning winger has taken a significant pay cut to play on home soil.

CHESLIN KOLBE ADDS TO CAR COLLECTION

On his Instagram account, Cheslin Kolbe shared a look at his latest ride – a sponsorship by Nissan to drive a brand new Navara Pro 4X, which can easily fetch up to R1 million.

The pint-size rugby player appeared minuscule behind the wheel of the monster double-cab bakkie.



Like the rugby player, his new wheels can take on any terrain.

Cheslin Kolbe’s latest addition comes just months after he showed off a R2 million Range Rover Defender 130.



The large black SUV is one of the “biggest and toughest” vehicles by the British manufacturer.

“Small guy, big dreams”, the pint-sized player captioned a clip of him taking off in the monstrous car.

Cheslin owns several high-performance vehicles, including a Nissan Skyline GT-R R34 and a BMW E92 M3.

‘MY WIFE AND KIDS’

Cheslin Kolbe’s new family-friendly car comes after he reunited with his wife and three children after living abroad in Japan, where he played for club Suntory Sungoliath, for several years.

The 32-year-old decided to return to South Africa – and take a significant pay cut – to be closer to his family.



He told the Cape Times: “Yes, the reason was to come back to play for the Stormers, where my rugby started. Hopefully, I can finish my career with the team as well. But the biggest part was for my wife and kids.

He continued: “Not being here with them, seeing them grow, was tough on us. Last year, I returned after six months of not seeing my children, Kylah, Mila and Cayden, and my boy almost didn’t recognise me. That made me realise it is time to come home and spend time with them.”

World.title: Dr Musa Mthombeni celebrates qualifying as a Neurointerventionist
World.content:
Media personality and qualified doctor Dr Musa Mthombeni has added another impressive achievement to his growing medical career. The Diagnostic and Interventional Radiologist recently announced that he is now officially a qualified Neurointerventionist after completing his sub-specialty training.

DR MUSA MTHOMBENI CELEBRATES A MAJOR MILESTONE

Taking to Instagram, Dr Musa Mthombeni proudly shared the news with his followers.

“Vukani! Sekunjalo! Daddies are up! After over a year of very early morning, parking lot complaints about people wanting to scratch my #Vclass, late nights in angiotheatre and probably consuming way too much cottee, I’ve officially wrapped up my sub-specialty training in Interventional Neuroradiology / Endovascular Neurosurgery.



Translation: I am now a fully qualified Neurointerventionist. Yes, you can trust me around your brain’s blood vessels. Phakathi inside!

I am so excited to step into this next chapter, apply these skills, and changing some lives in a field I have absolutely fallen in love with.”

A Neurointerventionist is a highly specialised doctor who diagnoses and treats conditions that affect the blood vessels in the brain, head, neck, and spine. These specialists often use minimally invasive procedures to treat conditions such as strokes, brain aneurysms, and other vascular disorders. Their work can help save lives and improve recovery outcomes for patients.

DR MUSA MTHOMBENI THANKS THOSE WHO SUPPORTED HIM

Dr Musa also used the moment to thank the people who stood by him throughout his training journey.

He wrote: “A big thank you to Dr Ro (If I know what I’m doing today, it’s entirely his fault), my colleagues, my mentors, my incredible wife (who deserves a medal for putting up with my fellowship schedule and me doing unscheduled DSAs every 2 days), and my family. I couldn’t have done it without your unwavering support-and your tolerance of me talking about blood vessels 24/7.



Time to get to work!”

His message highlighted the support he received from his mentors, colleagues, friends, and family during the demanding fellowship programme.

DR MUSA MTHOBENI CONTINUES TO GROW HIS MEDICAL CAREER

This latest achievement comes less than a year after another important academic milestone.

In July 2025, Dr Musa officially became a Master of Medicine graduate. He completed his Master of Medicine in Diagnostic Radiology from the University of the Witwatersrand (Wits).

His new qualification reflects years of hard work and commitment to medicine. While many South Africans know him as a media personality, Musa continues to build an impressive reputation in the healthcare field.

World.title: Gayton announces more FREE lucky fan trips to FIFA World Cup
World.content:
Gayton McKenzie has announced the next round of the 'lucky fan programme'. Images via X

Minister of Sport, Arts and Culture Gayton McKenzie has confirmed that the department will fund the trips of an additional 19 “lucky fans” to watch Bafana Bafana play their final FIFA World Cup group match next week.

The group, which includes well-known sports influencer Rory Petzer, will witness the South African national team face off against South Korea on Thursday, 25 June.

The match takes place at the Estadio BBVA in Monterrey, Mexico.



GAYTON MCKENZIE ANNOUNCES MORE LUCKY FANS’ TRIPS TO FIFA WORLD CUP

In a media statement, the Minister of Sport, Art and Culture, Gayton McKenzie, announced that the department would send 19 soccer fans to watch Bafana Bafana in action at the FIFA World Cup.

The delegation – made up of the biggest PSL club supporters – will fly to Mexico as part of the department’s “Lucky Fan programme”.

The group also includes several popular influencers, one of them being sports social media star Rory Petzer, known as “wild cards”.

Gayton previously claimed that the fan trip was funded by sponsors like Betway, Cell C and Honor.

The minister responded to a parliamentary question about the trip, stating that “no government funds were utilised directly for the Lucky Fans travel initiative”, adding that his department’s role was limited to the administration and facilitation of the competition.

Sponsors covered flights, accommodation, ground transport, and a daily allowance.



BAFANA BAFANA’S LAST DANCE?

While many have argued that the odds may be against them, Bafana Bafana’s path to getting out of the group stages and into the knockout stages is clear.

To advance to the next round, South Africa would have to finish in the top two places of Group A, which includes South Korea, Mexico and Czechia. Securing a third spot would also advance them, as eight of the best third-placed teams across all 12 groups will also advance to the Round of 32.

According to pundits, Bafana would need at least four points to progress out of the preliminary stage.

World.title: ‘Why not Pitso?’ Kaizer Chiefs supporters react to Da Cruz hiring
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs supporters have expressed mixed reactions following the appointment of Fernando Da Cruz as the club’s new head coach.

The French-Portuguese tactician was unveiled by Amakhosi on Wednesday evening, taking over from co-coaches Khalil Ben Youssef and Cedric Kaze.

In a statement confirming the appointment, Chiefs said:



“Kaizer Chiefs are pleased to confirm the appointment of Fernando Da Cruz as Head Coach.

“He has signed a two-year contract with a one-year option, effective 1 July 2026. Born in France, Da Cruz comes highly qualified with a UEFA Pro Licence, the highest coaching certification in football.”

Da Cruz is no stranger to Naturena. He spent time with the club during a pre-season camp two years ago before joining the Moroccan Football Federation, where he served as Technical Director until the end of June.

The 53-year-old will officially begin his duties on July 1 as Chiefs look to build on last season’s progress.

Da Cruz to take over as Kaizer Chiefs coach next month

His announcement sparked a variety of reactions from supporters on social media, with some welcoming the appointment while others questioned the club’s decision, believing former Mamelodi Sundowns coach Pitso Mosimane would have been a better choice.

@jtamz2 wrote: “Welcome Coach Da Cruz to the mighty Khosi. We wish you well as you build on the work done by the co-coaches.”



@Qabzo added: “Welcome back to the Khosi Nation, Coach Da Cruz. We must cruise nicely next season.”

Others were less convinced and felt Da Cruz won’t add much to Kaizer Chiefs.

@LeboThamage commented: “We never learn. Our problem is not the coaches, our management is the problem. How long are we going to keep changing coaches instead of fixing the real issue?”

@kwaNompondwana wrote: “I wonder if it means the players will be listening to the same tactics one more time, given the fact that he was working under Nabi. Nonetheless, welcome again Mr Da Cruz. Hopefully you’re bringing something different — winning.”

Kaizer Chiefs appoint Da Cruz but some fans question?

Meanwhile, @Musojnr questioned Da Cruz’s credentials, posting: “What has he won as a head coach? This plumber? I’ll listen on the radio.”

@EdwinMokhosi expressed his disappointment, saying: “I love this team with all my heart, but I think it’s time to pack my bags. You have Pitso Mosimane, a proven winner, and you go for this one who came with Nabi and left for greener pastures. We are not ready to be the best in Africa.”

Will Da Cruz bring joy to Naturena?

World.title: Home Affairs deports Nigerian family denied asylum in Ireland
World.content:
A Nigeria family have been sent back to Nigeria after they were deported to South Africa. Images via Canva

A Nigerian family that was denied asylum in Ireland and deported to South Africa have been sent back to Nigeria, Minister of Home Affairs Leon Schreiber has confirmed.

Foreign national Titilayo Oluwakemi Oyekanmi and her three sons fled SA, in which they have permanent residency, after they claimed that a gang had beaten them.

Irish authorities formally rejected their bid for humanitarian protection.



SA DEPORTS NIGERIAN FAMILY DENIED ASYLUM IN IRELAND

In a recent parliamentary response on the case, Minister of Home Affairs Leon Schreiber confirmed that the Nigerian family who were denied asylum in Ireland and were deported to South Africa were sent back to Nigeria.

The Minister confirmed that Titilayo Oluwakemi Oyekanmi and her three sons were taken to Lindela Holding Facility upon their arrival at OR Tambo International Airport.

The family were deported to South Africa – their country of permanent residency – in February after a crackdown on illegal immigration, including those who had ignored deportation orders.

Schreiber said: “The Nigerian Embassy identified and issued travel documents, and they were returned to Nigeria within 72 hours of their arrival”.

The Department of Home Affairs has confirmed that the Nigerian family deported from Ireland earlier this year was taken into custody upon arrival at OR Tambo International Airport.

Responding to questions raised by ATM, the department stated that the family was transferred to… pic.twitter.com/oA7KJsMrq8  June 12, 2026

According to the Irish Times, Nigerian woman Oyekanmi and her three sons fled South Africa for Ireland after she claimed that a criminal gang in South Africa brutally beat her. She told the media and protest groups that she had feared for the lives of her children.

She and her children arrived in Ireland in 2023, seeking asylum. However, her application was denied, and so was an appeal.

Under the Department of Justice, it was found that authorities were not convinced that the family qualified for refugee protection or that they could not live safely in South Africa.

RULE OF LAW

In recent weeks, South Africa has witnessed a significant increase in both government-led repatriations and the deportation of foreign nationals. This has also included voluntary repatriation efforts by foreign governments in response to xenophobic violence and anti-migrant protests across the country.

Minister of Home Affairs Leon Schreiber has said that his department is committed to enforcing SA’s immigration laws and restoring the rule of law.

He said in a recent statement: “Our ongoing orderly and lawful deportations and repatriations, which have increased by 46% over the past two years, is clear evidence of this.”

Schreiber called on South Africans to “never engage in violence or take the law into their own hands”.

World.title: WEATHER: Cold, cloudy conditions with showers expected

Cold, cloudy conditions with showers expected across parts of South Africa. Image: File

KWAZULU-NATAL

KwaZulu-Natal will see morning and evening fog patches over the interior, while the rest of the province stays partly cloudy and cool to cold.

Forecasters expect isolated showers and rain over the far eastern parts, as well as along the coast and nearby inland areas, where cloud cover will be more persistent.

The UVB sunburn index will remain high.
